intent: POST /api/missions with an unrecognised dispatchMode returned 201 and dispatched the mission immediately. The operator asked for a schedule and got an unattended run. Reported as the only release-blocker of the 2026-08-30 QA pass, and confirmed as such.
invariants: I1 A dispatchMode that was SUPPLIED and is unrecognised is refused with a 400 naming the four legal values.
I2 An ABSENT dispatchMode still means now. That is a legacy contract asserted over HTTP by full-stack-smoke.mjs, so a blanket not-valid check would have been wrong.
I3 A refusal leaves NO mission row. The row was written twenty lines before the mode was read.
I4 cron with no schedule is its own 400, not a fall-through to run-now.
I5 A template cannot store an invalid mode, which is what made this UI-reachable.
I6 A failed immediate dispatch is not audited as ok:true.
root_cause: dispatch.ts destructured parseDispatchMode as isSaveMode/isQueueMode/isCronMode and dropped the valid flag that exists for exactly this. The run-now branch is written as a NEGATIVE, so it is the else-of-everything rather than an explicit isNowMode test, and any string the four comparisons miss lands there. dispatch-mode.ts's own header says the flag lets callers write if-not-valid-return-error; of its two callers, promote did and dispatch did not. The route validates its outer action vocabulary with a default 400 and then hands an unvalidated inner enum to a handler that treats unrecognised as run-it.
beyond_the_report: cron with a missing or empty schedule un-sets isCronMode and takes the identical run-now path. The client has refused that since T-0063; the API did not.

Templates persist an arbitrary dispatchMode (the action body is typed any, update writes the field unvalidated) and useMissionComposer casts it back into form state, so a poisoned template plus Apply plus submit was an immediate unattended run. That is what turned an API-only defect into a UI-reachable one.
The template's stored type was save|now|cron, missing queue, drifted from DispatchMode. Aliased to the real type now.
dispatchMissionNow's result was discarded and the audit line hardcoded ok:true, so a dispatch that had already flipped the mission to failed was recorded as a success.
oracle_provenance: Committed alone at 7142f462 ahead of the implementation at 9f100455. Measured against dev@07e36857: 15 red, 5 green. The greens are the legal-mode controls, and one is load-bearing: the ABSENT-mode contract. Pinning it meant the obvious fix would go red in the unit suite rather than silently breaking the integration smoke.
verification: Five mutations, all caught, including the one that matters most: treating absent as invalid turns the legacy-contract control red. Proved end to end against a real server on a temp HERMES_HOME: four invalid cases answered 400 with precise messages, four legal modes and the absent-mode case answered 201, and the missions list held EXACTLY five rows for five successful dispatches, so none of the four refusals left an orphan. Gate: lint 0, tsc 0, 3340 tests / 387 suites, knip 0, canary 0, build 0.
